correctness.rationale: An exact orientation-by-orientation active-edge derivative identity yields the sharp coefficient. The scalar minimization of \(s^{p-1}+(1-s)^{p-1}\) is proved by strict convexity/concavity for every real \(1<p<\infty\). A feasible data vector attains the coefficient for every blade, proving necessity and sharpness; standard maximum-principle and dissipativity arguments yield existence and uniqueness even for \(1<p<2\); the upper Dini derivative gives global sufficiency. The graph-size phase diagram and nonlinear scaling-rate divergence follow algebraically. The 108 exact witness tests and 2536 rational-grid finite tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The graph family is a natural clique-sum/windmill construction, and the invariant measures actual edgewise steepness of individual nonlinear diffusion signals. A complete exact classification holds uniformly over all real \(p\) and all blade multiplicities, exhibits a genuinely p-sensitive critical threshold even for fixed graph, and separates one-input contraction from stronger two-input semigroup stability. These are structurally motivated phenomena, not a small-instance table or a trivial substitution.
